Decided 2026-07-28 (resolves the "ext-agents UNRESOLVED" from the connect-surface merge): MCP clients (ChatGPT/Claude/CLI) are **external agents**, not connectors.

- **Rejected**: static `mcp` connector definition + connection-per-grant + write-path connection_id stamping. Also rejected earlier: schema-level merge (no FK between oauth_clients and connections).
- **Chosen shape (NOT BUILT)**: Agents page gains an "External agents" section (client groups from the existing clients API, visually distinct — no model/guardrail affordances, since binding is attribution NOT authz per [[project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz]]). Detail page: sessions (#2239 endpoint), activity (events by client_id), access/revoke moved from Connectors → Apps (`/$owner/connectors/apps`), which then retires.
- **Also unbuilt**: the `clientId` events-filter gap in owletto `event-filters.ts` (server `client_ids` on read_knowledge/get_content is DONE since #2211). ~40 lines; needed for "click client → its event trail" deep links into `/activity`.

Why ChatGPT shows no conversations in memory: MCP is pull-only — its 629 events are 455 tool-invocation audits + config changes, zero conversation content. Lever for capturing takeaways = MCP server instructions telling clients to call save_memory.

name: reference_mcp_client_identity_and_attribution
description: "How an MCP client is identified (6 signals on oauth_clients + events.client_id), the display-name precedence conflict between two surfaces, and the fact that conversations carries NO client attribution — measured on prod 2026-07-30"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:14:41.638Z
---

## ChatGPT DOES create conversations — I was wrong twice

Measured on prod 2026-07-30. Do not repeat the claim that MCP clients only call
read tools; it is false.

```
ChatGPT | run_sdk 498 · query_sql 123 · query_sdk 32 · search_sdk 28 · search_memory 6 · save_memory 2
Claude  | run_sdk 1244 · query_sql 1224 · …
```

Of ChatGPT's `run_sdk` calls, **13 are `conversations.send`** — real agent
conversations. One is live in the listing right now:
`personal-agent_8a2D2Yb…_8dc12bdd…_mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5`, surfaced as
`{"id":"mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5","platform":"web"}`. ChatGPT's dominant SDK path
is `operations.execute` (539) — it drives the Chrome extension.

Method that works: `events` JOIN `oauth_clients` on `e.client_id`, then
`jsonb_array_elements(payload_data->'sdk_call_trace')` for `path` and `args`.
`conversations` itself is NOT in the MCP query allowlist.

## The six identity signals

Five on `oauth_clients`, one per-invocation:

| signal | when written | ChatGPT's value |
|---|---|---|
| `client_name` | DCR registration | `ChatGPT` |
| `metadata.last_client_info.name/title` | MCP `initialize`, per session | `openai-mcp` |
| `metadata.last_user_agent` | HTTP header | `openai-mcp/1.0.0` |
| `software_id` / `software_version` | DCR software statement | null |
| `redirect_uris` host | OAuth callback | `chatgpt.com` |
| `events.client_id` | every tool call | the only PER-INVOCATION signal |

Also `metadata.last_capabilities` — ChatGPT alone declares `openai/visibility`
and `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. `recordMcpClientActivity`
(`mcp-handler.ts:619` → `touchClientActivity`) writes the first three on every
authenticated request.

## Two surfaces disagree on the name

`client-routes.ts:258` uses `clientInfo.name || client_name` — clientInfo WINS.
`client-session-routes.ts` joins `oauth_clients.client_name` — the opposite.
**5 of 19 prod rows display a different vendor than they registered as**, because
clientInfo reflects the process driving the connection, not the app:

```
Owletto for Mac → claude-code   (×3)
Lobu CLI        → claude-code
Claude          → claude-code
```

Trustworthy identity = `redirect_uris` host + `software_id` (can't be
self-reported away). `clientInfo` answers "what is driving it" — a different
question worth its own field, not an override.

## The attribution gap

`events.client_id` knows. **`conversations` does not** — the write path stores
`kind='owned'` → `platform:'web'` and drops the client. So ChatGPT, Claude, the
CLI and the browser all land in one undifferentiated bucket, and no query can
separate them. This is why there is no ChatGPT icon in Recent, and it is the same
missing field as the shared-thread attribution gap. Fix = `conversations.client_id`
written where the run is minted.

## last_seen_at exists; agent scoping does not

`oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is live on all 19 prod rows (Claude 17:43,
ChatGPT 17:10 on 2026-07-30) — the MCP equivalent of
`watchers.last_run_completed_at` already exists, no migration needed.

But `metadata.last_agent_id` is **NULL on all 19 rows**, so
`client-routes.ts:255` (`if (agentId && assignedAgentId !== agentId) return null`)
drops every client from any agent-scoped view.

**Root cause traced 2026-07-30 — not a bug, an opt-in nobody opts into.**
`authCtx.agentId` IS set, by `syncAgentBinding` (`mcp-handler.ts:842`) from
`authCtx.requestedAgentId`. That comes ONLY from the `x-lobu-agent-id` header or
a JSON body field (`mcp-handler.ts:421`, `:452`) — **never from the URL**. Mounts
are just `/mcp`, `/mcp/`, `/mcp/:orgSlug`, `/mcp/:orgSlug/`
(`index.ts:2766-2769`); no agent segment exists. Hosted clients send no header,
so `requestedAgentId` is null and `touchClientActivity` skips `last_agent_id`.

FIX (user-approved 2026-07-30): add `/mcp/:orgSlug/:agentId`. It feeds the
existing `requestedAgentId` path and `syncAgentBinding` already validates the
agent exists in the org. Safe because MCP binding is attribution, not
authorization — see [[project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz]].

Related: [[project_recent_feed_unified]],
[[project_mcp_clients_as_external_agents]],
[[reference_behavior_conversation_id_is_client_forgeable]].

name: project_connect_surface_merge
description: "REVISED x3 2026-07-27 — 2 tabs (Connectors/Runtime), Models just-in-time, no status tab; external-agents-in-Runtime UNRESOLVED"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08a3b00f-d798-4b3e-89c3-c9b62c54a2fa
  modified: 2026-07-27T16:59:42.262Z
---

Proposal to collapse Connectors + Models + Sandboxes + Devices into one surface at `/connect/*`. Designed 2026-07-27, **not built**. Spec artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/eb23eeaf-922a-4e9e-b9dd-56a73bf6baa4

**Why it holds up (structural evidence, not taste):**
- `DeviceWorkerItem` already lives in `packages/owletto/src/lib/api/connections.ts` — not a devices module — and carries `connector_count`, `connector_error_count`, `connectors[]`.
- `AgentProviderCatalogItem` (`lib/api/agents.ts`) has `installed`, `authType`, `description`, `iconUrl` — near-identical to `ConnectorDefinitionItem`.
- `SandboxItem.connected` means "required credential exists in the vault" — the same question `connection.status` answers.
- All four are: browse a catalog → authenticate → get an instance → watch it run. The split is four pages that grew separately and got a shared `ConnectTabBar` bolted on later (`src/lib/connect-tabs.ts` already calls the group "Connect").

**FINAL SHAPE 2026-07-27 (3rd revision).** Two tabs inside the single "Connect" sidebar row:
- **Connectors** — what an agent can reach. Device-provided connectors (Screen Time, Photos, Bookmarks) ALSO listed here read-only with their host named ("via Burak's MacBook"); not-addable and not-listed are different things.
- **Runtime** — devices + sandboxes (this merge is well-founded and cheap).
- **No status/attention tab** — broken rows sort to the top of their own tab; a dedicated tab would sit empty.
- **Models LEAVES the tab bar** — a tab advertises a required setup step, and models are optional on SaaS (`hasSystemKey()`); reached just-in-time via `agent-error-cta.ts`. CAVEAT: `hasSystemKey()` is deployment state — self-hosted OSS may have NO platform key, making Models step one. Evidence-gated, see below.

**Sidebar reality (I got this wrong for most of the session):** `OWNER_SECTIONS` has exactly TWO entries — Memory and Connect (`segments: ["connectors","infrastructure"]`) — then an Agents roster, then Recent. Connect is ONE row above the roster, framed in-code as "workspace plumbing". So the "does this read as an agent harness?" worry is a non-issue; everything designed here lives inside one sidebar row.

**UNRESOLVED — external MCP clients under Runtime.** Adversarial review rejected it: devices/sandboxes are substrates Lobu *dispatches work onto*; an MCP client *initiates requests into* Lobu — authorized, not provisioned. "Where it runs" is literally false for it. Also mixes resource instances (Burak's MacBook) with client classes (Claude Code). Proposed compromise: stateless **setup recipes** can live in Runtime (`DeviceTarget` and MCP `InstallTarget` are the same shape, and `lobu login` is already both); stateful **connected client instances** belong in an Access/Connected-clients surface. Hinges on whether users read an MCP client as "where my agent works from" or "a thing I granted access to" — not a code question.

**User decisions — what SURVIVES the revision:** landing shows what's CONNECTED (not catalog-first); **deployments fold-in goes FIRST**. What does NOT survive: the full `/connect/*` move (dropped — largest work, least evidence, and the win was tidiness) and "uniform rows, kind is a label" (too strong — a device row NAVIGATES, a sandbox row does not; uniform *appearance*, not uniform *behaviour*).

**Merge the LIST, keep DETAIL views distinct** — connections/feeds, API keys/model lists, permissions/pairing are genuinely different shapes.

**The five-state vocabulary is WRONG — superseded 2026-07-27 (external review, accepted).** working/attention/installed-idle/available/managed collapses THREE orthogonal axes: **provisioning** (available|installed), **health** (working|attention), **ownership** (self|managed). They vary independently, so the enum cannot express "managed AND failing" (a delegated connector whose owning org revoked it — real), "degraded/partial" (1 of 2 Slack workspaces expired), pending/validating, rate-limited, or stale/unknown. Model the four fields separately and DERIVE the row label. A new case then adds a derivation, not a 6th enum value every surface must re-handle.

**Model + sandbox detail pages are FLAT — no tabs.** A credential + a short list is one subject. Tabs only where there is genuinely more than one (connector: Overview/Feeds/Actions/Settings; device: Runs/Connectors/Permissions). Sharpens the open question: neither may deserve a route at all — both could be drawers on the list.

**Blast radius is the one addition that makes this superior rather than tidier.** Show what depends on each row ("12 agents", "4 behaviors") and sort attention rows BY it — a rejected model key outranks an offline laptop. Severity is a property of what sits downstream, not of the row. Without it a merged list is an inventory; with it, it is triage.

**Blockers / traps:**
- `chrome-extension` is NOT in the frontend platform union (`ios|android|macos|windows|linux`) — 4 Chrome connectors won't typecheck until widened.
- The rail means two things: on a connector it drills INTO children (connections); on models/devices it switches between SIBLINGS. Same position, different relation.
- Two rail sides exist today: connector pages use a LEFT rail; the device page uses a 360px RIGHT sidebar. Merging forces one (left).
- Kind vs facet are different axes — "chat" is what it does, "device" is where it runs. WhatsApp is both (cloud API + local Mac). A row must be allowed in two buckets.
- Device rows are two different things: "Lobu for Mac" is the runtime you install, "Reminders" is a connector it provides. Flat listing makes the app look like a peer of what it hosts.
- The built-in sandbox must NOT be a row — it's in `SandboxesPayload` but the current page never renders it. Listing it invites a "disconnect" that isn't real.
- "Managed" state (someone else owns the credential): public-org delegated connectors, `systemAvailable` model keys, cross-org device grants. Each surface answers this differently today; a merge forces one answer.

**Rail is one tree across 3 levels** (connector → connection → feed) and descending "only moves the highlight" — `$connectorKey.$connectionId.tsx` renders the same `ConnectorSourcesRail`. Feeds belong to the CONNECTION, not the connector. This survives the merge unchanged.

**Route name is `create`, NOT `add`** — `/$owner/connectors/create` + `create.$connectorKey.tsx` already exist. Page title is "Add a connection".

**Install ≠ connect.** `install_connector` enables a DEFINITION and explicitly "does not authenticate external accounts"; `connect` separately creates a connection. Takes exactly ONE of `connector_id` | `source_url` | `source_uri` | `source_code` | `mcp_url`. The web UI exposes two via ONE auto-detecting field: URLs ending `.ts`/`.js` → `source_url`, anything else → probed as `mcp_url` (`connection-form.tsx:804-846`). `source_uri`/`source_code` are CLI/agent only.

**Clicking an uninstalled catalog connector shows a PREVIEW screen with an explicit install button** (`use-installable-connector-selection.ts`): `installed === false && installable` → preview → install from the catalog entry's `source_uri` → reload catalog → verify it came back installed → THEN configuration. Already-installed connectors skip straight to configure. Failure path: a catalog entry with no `source_uri` errors "missing a source URI".

**Sandbox add = provider dropdown + that provider's fields.** `PROVIDER_FIELDS` in `$owner/environments/index.tsx`: default is a single `apiKey`; `vercel` needs `token`+`teamId`+`projectId`. That's the whole flow — hence the sandbox subpage is probably a drawer, not a route.

**Device pairing already exists** in `src/components/devices/device-connect.tsx` — THREE runtimes, not two: macOS app (PRIVATE BETA → "Contact us", `MAC_CONTACT_URL = https://lobu.ai/schedule`), Chrome extension ("Add to Chrome", real web store link), CLI (`npm i -g @lobu/cli && lobu login`). Three different verbs; a single "Install" label would be wrong. User's idea: surface these in the device rail as "Bring your own" under the paired devices.

**Device connectors (Screen Time, Photos…) are not CATALOG rows** — they AUTO-WIRE when a paired device advertises the capability, so an "Add" button would have nothing to do. The catalog lists the 3 runtimes instead. **BUT they must still be VISIBLE under Connectors** with their device named (revised 2026-07-27): a user asking "what can my agent read" looks in Connectors, and hiding them only under Runtime means searching "Screen Time" finds nothing. Not-addable and not-listed are different things — this was the hole in the original three-tab split.

## The narrow "Runtime" cut — DO THIS FIRST (session f79c5bac, verified 2026-07-27)

Fold **Sandboxes + Devices → one "Runtime" tab**. Connect goes 4 tabs → 3: **Connectors, Models, Runtime** = what you connect to, what thinks, where it runs. ~4 files changed, 2 new. Ships value without waiting on the permission question, and de-risks the full merge by proving its two hard problems cheaply.

Why it's coherent: the two ledes already say the same thing from opposite ends — sandboxes are "remote sandbox providers your agents can execute in *instead of the built-in local runtime*"; devices "run device-bound connectors". Remote vs local runtime. Both already render through the same `InfraTabScaffold`.

**The asymmetry — a device row NAVIGATES, a sandbox row does NOT:**
| | Devices | Sandboxes |
|---|---|---|
| Row | `<Link>` → `devices/$deviceId` | `<div>` + inline delete/confirm |
| Add | `DeviceConnect` (pairing) | `CreateSandboxForm` (credential) |
| Scope | user-private, cross-workspace | org-scoped |
| Detail | separate route | expands in place |

So "uniform rows" means uniform **appearance**, not uniform **behaviour**. Sort devices first (they already have a "Yours · private" badge) above org sandboxes.

**Verified traps (re-checked against the repo, not taken on trust):**
- `InfraTabScaffold` takes ONE `addLabel: string` + ONE `onStartAdd: () => void` + one empty state. Two kinds = two Add flows. Extend it with an action array (Models still needs the single-action form) or drop it here.
- **Second mount point:** `SandboxesBody` is DEFINED in `$owner/environments/index.tsx` and imported by `infrastructure/sandboxes.tsx`. A merge scoped to `/infrastructure` leaves `/environments` on the old surface.
- `?provider=` deep link: `sandboxes.tsx` has `validateSearch` + auto-opens the create form with a prefill banner. New route needs the same, and the redirect must FORWARD the param.
- Independent empty states — "No runtimes" with a paired Mac but no Modal credential is a lie. Empty only when BOTH are.
- `src/app/index.tsx` hand-builds a device-detail URL → redirects from both old paths are mandatory. `routeTree.gen.ts` regenerates. `all-routes.test.tsx` + `owner-root-redirect.test.tsx` both need updating.


## Verified backend facts (re-checked 2026-07-27; two of these correct earlier claims)

- **Connected MCP clients ALREADY have list + revoke.** `DELETE /mcp/:clientId` at `packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts:302`, plus `lobu clients revoke` in the CLI (kills tokens AND live sessions). I had claimed "no revoke route" — that was over-generalised from the PAT case and is WRONG for OAuth clients. Only the **web UI** is missing.
- **PATs are a different asset class.** `PersonalAccessTokenService.revoke()` at `auth/tokens.ts:174` with no HTTP route found. Do not collapse PATs, OAuth clients and messaging identities into one list — messaging identities deliberately have NO revoke (they are platform users).
- **Devices are ORG-attached, not user-private.** `DeviceWorkerItem` carries `organization_id` and NO `user_id`; the comment says "Workspace this device is attached to". The "Yours · private / follows you across workspaces" grouping came from a prior session's summary and I repeated it in two artifacts unverified. Group Runtime by KIND.
- **MCP install registry already exists, hidden.** `mcp-install-targets.ts` has 6 targets (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, Skills) + `buildMcpUrl(orgSlug)` → `/mcp/{slug}`. Used in exactly ONE place: a line inside `device-connect.tsx`. `DeviceTarget` and `InstallTarget` are the SAME shape — collapse them.
- **Dynamic client registration** at `POST /oauth/register` (documented at `GET /auth.md`) — no allowlist, so "custom MCP client" is instructions, not a record you create.
- **Routes that break on a rename** (all invisible to a refactor, must be repointed FIRST): `infrastructure.tsx:8` redirects bare `/infrastructure` → `sandboxes` (a route being deleted); `agent-error-cta.ts:72` builds `/{slug}/infrastructure/models` — that IS the just-in-time path the plan depends on; `app/index.tsx:108` string-concatenates a device URL.
- **Second double-mount found:** `InferenceProvidersBody` is defined in `inference-providers/index.tsx` and re-mounted at `infrastructure/models` — same trap as `SandboxesBody` in `environments/index.tsx`.

**Agent binding over MCP is attribution only** — see [[project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz]]. This is the most serious finding of the session and gates the connected-clients UI.

**Spec artifact (current):** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/d6869bcf-580a-413a-ab50-bd8c306a296c — has a HAVE/GAP table (7 HAVE / 11 GAP) and a 10-step sequence. Superseded drafts kept as record: merged-list `eb23eeaf`, three-tab `5c04b35d`.

---
name: feedback-design-review-before-implementing
description: Read the substrate and get the design reviewed BEFORE writing code — make review is diff-scoped and cannot catch design flaws early
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 5d06133d-7c19-4807-81f8-78f582615802
  modified: 2026-07-29T18:30:56.142Z
---

Before implementing anything that touches an existing subsystem, (1) READ that subsystem's
source — not my model of it — and (2) put the written design through a reviewer (codex) BEFORE
writing code. `make review` is diff-scoped and post-hoc: by construction it can only review code
that already exists, so every design flaw it finds costs a full review + CI round.

**Why:** PR #2315 (claim-side recycle) took 12 review rounds, 8 of which found real defects. The
gate's own logic was right from round 1 and barely changed. What broke eight separate times was
its interaction with substrate I had never read:
- queue retry/attempt semantics (`claimOne`, `scheduleRetry`) → rounds 9, 10
- claim ordering: `scheduleRetry` moves `run_at`, so a deferral reorders the lane → round 8
- SSE reconnect replay re-enqueues a running turn's durable input → rounds 1, 3
- marker sweep behaviour on rebuild failure → round 5
- replica concurrency: claims do NOT process in `runs.id` order → round 11
- conversation advisory lock released mid-recycle → another pod wins the handoff → round 12

I first opened `runs-queue.ts` at round 8. Reading it first would have collapsed rounds 8/9/10
into one design decision (the deferral mechanism must not be the retry mechanism — obvious the
moment you look at the SQL).

**How to apply:**
1. List the subsystems the change touches. Read their source (especially the SQL and the error
   paths) before writing a line.
2. Write the design down, then hand it to codex as a DESIGN review. Iterate there — it is far
   cheaper than iterating on a posted `make review`.
3. Only then implement. `make review-fix` → `make review` ONCE stays the tail of the flow.
4. Recurring defect class in this program: **distinct failure modes collapsed into one outcome**
   (rounds 6, 9, 12). When any error path is added, enumerate EVERY error reachable there and
   classify each explicitly: deliver / defer / terminalize / propagate. A bare `catch (error)`
   over a multi-error operation is the smell.

See [[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]] (two rounds of the same root-cause class → stop
and audit the substrate, don't run another round) and
[[project_deployment_recycle_redesign]] for the program this came from.

name: feedback_dont_overconsolidate_surfaces
description: "Similar data shapes are not evidence two things belong on one page — merge by user intent, not by struct similarity"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 08a3b00f-d798-4b3e-89c3-c9b62c54a2fa
  modified: 2026-07-27T17:11:10.672Z
---

Do not argue for merging two surfaces because their types look alike. On 2026-07-27 I proposed folding Models into a merged Connect surface because `AgentProviderCatalogItem` has the same fields as `ConnectorDefinitionItem`. The user pushed back and was right: a model provider is *what thinks*, a connector is *what you reach*, a sandbox/device is *where it runs*. Similar fields, different questions.

**The test:** can you describe the grouping out loud without a conjunction? "Connect to / thinks / runs" passes. "Connectors, models, sandboxes and devices" is a list, not a category.

**Also: separate the GOAL from one implementation of it.** The real win was "an operator can see everything broken in one place." I assumed that required merging the pages, and designed the expensive version. A cross-cutting attention view across three tabs delivers the same win without flattening anything. Ask what the goal needs before assuming it needs the big change.

**Landing shape for Lobu (2026-07-27):** three tabs — Connectors, Models, Runtime (= sandboxes + devices, both answer "where does my agent execute"). Plus one attention view spanning all three. Device-provided connectors (Screen Time, Photos) must ALSO appear under Connectors with their device named — a device is two things, a runtime you install and a source of connectors, and a clean three-way split otherwise hides them from anyone searching for what their agent can read.

Related: [[project_connect_surface_merge]], [[feedback_check_prior_sessions_before_designing]], [[feedback_structural_not_usage_deletion_evidence]]

content.text:
I read the actual substrate (routes, device registration, client routes, the connectors list synthesis) rather than reasoning from the page names. Here's what's really there and what I'd build.

## The three things you named are not one kind

| Thing | What it creates | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Owletto Mac app | `device_workers` row (`platform=macos`) **+** an `oauth_clients` row | Lobu dispatches work **out** to it; it *provides* connectors |
| Owletto Chrome ext | `device_workers` row (`platform=chrome-extension`) | same — provides `browser.*` connectors |
| Lobu CLI | `oauth_clients` / PAT **only** — `cli`/`node` is not in `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST` (`packages/core/src/capabilities.ts:59`) | it calls **into** Lobu |
| ChatGPT / Claude | `oauth_clients` | calls **into** Lobu |

So: **yes for Mac and Chrome, no for the CLI.** A paired Mac already materializes real connector definitions in your org (`device-reconcile.ts` → `ensureDeviceConnectorWired`, driven by `connector_manifests` on each poll) — Screen Time, Photos, Calendar are already rows in `/connectors`. The device is the runtime hosting them. The CLI creates no connection, no feed, no action; it's a credential holder. Calling it a connector says "your agent can reach this", which is backwards.

## Target shape

**Devices become rows in the connectors list — under the `runtime` facet that already exists.** This isn't an analogy; a paired Mac is the local counterpart of a remote sandbox, and sandboxes are already synthesized into that list as `sandbox:{id}` rows (`lib/connectors/sandbox-rows.ts`). Add `buildDeviceConnectorRows` alongside it, one row per device instance:

```
Burak's MacBook    [Runtime] [On device]   macOS · 5 connectors · online
Chrome             [Runtime] [On device]   1 connector · offline 2h
Vercel             [Runtime]               vercel · Connected
```

Detail mounts at `/connectors/device:{id}` — `$connectorKey.index.tsx` already branches on `inference:` / `sandbox:` prefixes, so today's 404-line device detail (runs, capabilities, rename, delete, pinned connections) moves in rather than dying. `/connectors/runtime/*` is deleted outright.

**Install instructions move into the catalog.** `DeviceConnect`'s four accordions (Mac / Chrome / CLI / Docker) become `install:*` catalog entries in `/connectors/create`, using the exact `sandbox-provider:` mechanic — picking one opens a locked panel showing instructions instead of a form. Same place you'd add the MCP-client recipes (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex) with `buildMcpUrl(orgSlug)` — that's `lobu memory configure --url` in GUI form, and it's the acquisition question the catalog is for.

DX delta on the journey you care about: connecting Claude Code goes from *user menu → My devices → CLI accordion → copy a 3-line command* to *Connect → Add → search "Claude Code"*.

**MCP clients get a section, not a page.** Bottom of `/connectors`, below the connector list, its own heading — "apps that hold a key to this workspace", last-seen + Revoke. `/connectors/apps` is deleted. I'd keep it visually separate rather than interleaved: revoking a person's grant and deleting an org connection are different danger classes, and the list's lede ("tools your agents use") stops being true if clients are mixed in.

Note this **reverses the 2026-07-28 decision** to put MCP clients on the Agents page as "External agents". I think Connect is the better home — an external agent with no model, no guardrails, no behaviors has to be rendered "visually distinct" from every other row on the Agents page, which is a tell it's in the wrong place. Your call, though; both kill the route.

## Sequencing — 4 PRs, one concern each

**PR1 (prerequisite): fix client identity.** `client-routes.ts:258` uses `clientInfo.name || client_name` — clientInfo wins, so in prod **Lobu CLI, Owletto for Mac ×3 and Claude all display as "claude-code"**, and `isFirstPartyLobuClient` therefore evaluates false for exactly the apps this plan needs to identify. Identity = `client_name` + `redirect_uris` host; `clientInfo` becomes a separate `drivenBy` field. Without this, the new section mislabels 5 of 19 prod rows and the device/client dedupe below has no signal to key off.

**PR2: devices → connectors list.** New `lib/connectors/device-rows.ts`; device detail moves under `$connectorKey`; delete `runtime.tsx`, `runtime/devices.tsx`, `runtime/index.tsx`, `runtime/devices/$deviceId.tsx`; repoint 8 call sites (`app/index.tsx:107` hand-builds the URL, `connection-form.tsx:781,1413`, `connection-settings-tab.tsx:450`, `connection-feed-detail.tsx:83`, `$connectorKey.index.tsx:1080,1241`, sidebar user menu); redirects for both old paths (precedent exists — `/environments`, `memory-legacy-redirects`).

**PR3: catalog install recipes.** `DeviceConnect` → `install:*` entries; "Add device" CTAs repoint to `/connectors/create?filter=device` (which lands on instructions, strictly better than today's list).

**PR4: connected-apps section.** Move `groupClients` out of the route file into `lib/clients/` (its test already imports across that boundary), delete `apps.tsx`, repoint `client-sessions-timeline.tsx:63` and the user-menu entry.

## Two traps that need your call

**Device scoping is user-owned, page is org-owned.** `GET /api/me/devices` filters `WHERE dw.user_id = $me` and returns devices across *all* your workspaces. Drop them onto an org page unchanged and you're rendering a cross-org personal list in a shared surface. My v1: filter client-side to `organization_id === current org`. Cost: a teammate's paired Mac stays invisible even though its connectors run in your org. Proper fix is an org-scoped device endpoint (owner name shown, admin-only delete, owner-only rename) — worth a follow-up, not worth blocking on.

**The Mac is both a device and an oauth client**, with no FK between the tables. It'll appear twice unless suppressed. Rule: hide a first-party client row when a device row exists for the same user+platform — which only works after PR1.

One thing that gets worse and you should decide you're okay with: `/connectors` becomes a page where a shared screenshot shows "Burak's MacBook".

---

**Confidence: high (85) on the taxonomy and the file-level plan** — I read `capabilities.ts`, `poll.ts`, `device-reconcile.ts`, `client-routes.ts`, the connectors index synthesis, and grepped every entry point to both routes. **Medium (60) on the connected-apps placement** — it reverses a documented adversarially-reviewed decision, and I'm arguing from DX judgment, not evidence. Nothing here is built or booted.

4. Confirm the v1 device-scoping compromise (yours-in-this-org) vs holding PR2 for the org-scoped endpoint.

Both `codex exec` and `pi -p` (the AI coding-assistant CLIs we lean on for review/dispatch) wait on stdin by default. When invoked via Bash with `run_in_background: true` or in any non-tty context **without** `< /dev/null`, the process blocks in S state at 0% CPU, makes no model API calls, and produces no output — looks "still processing" but is actually hung.

**Affected tools:** every CLI that reads stdin for interactive multiline input. Confirmed: `codex exec`, `pi -p`. Likely: any AI assistant in `--print` / non-interactive mode that still falls back to stdin if it's not closed.

**Symptoms (same for both):**
- Process visible in `ps` as S state, 0:00 CPU time stays flat
- No output written to the redirect target file
- `lsof -p <pid>` shows stdin still open (a tty or /dev/null inherited from parent)
- Burned 29 min waiting on codex, repeated mistake with pi after fixing landing branch — both hung silently

**How to apply:**

Every backgrounded `codex exec`:
```bash
codex exec --config model_reasoning_effort=high "PROMPT" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tail -N
```

Every backgrounded `pi -p`:
```bash
pi -p "PROMPT" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tail -N
```

Round 1 of a session is sometimes lucky (inherited tty from terminal); round 2+ reliably hangs. Don't rely on luck. Treat `< /dev/null` as mandatory for both.

**If you forget:** the process is killable with `kill <pid>`. Re-invoke with `< /dev/null`. Don't waste time troubleshooting the model / network / API key — it's almost always this.

Related: [[feedback_e2e_before_merge]] — the pattern "verify via second tool" only helps if the second tool actually runs.

# DESIGN: collapse `/connectors/runtime` (devices) + `/connectors/apps` (MCP clients) into `/connectors`

Status: DESIGN, not built. Repo: lobu (bun workspace, `packages/owletto` = React SPA frontend
submodule, `packages/server` = Hono gateway).

## Goal

Delete two owletto routes and fold everything they do into the single `/connectors` surface:

- `/$owner/connectors/runtime` + `/runtime/devices/$deviceId` — "My devices" (pair a Mac /
  Chrome extension / CLI / Docker; list paired devices; device detail).
- `/$owner/connectors/apps` — "Connected apps" (MCP clients over OAuth: ChatGPT, Claude, Lobu
  CLI) with a Revoke button.

User-stated intent: "put lobu cli, owletto chrome extension and owletto macos app in the
connectors [catalog] and just give them the instructions; when they're connected chrome
extension and mac show up as a connector/connection." Plus: MCP clients become rows under
Connectors that open a detail on click. Ship as ONE PR.

## Substrate as it actually is (read, not assumed)

### The connectors list is already a synthesized union

`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/index.tsx` builds `items` from three sources:

1. real connector definitions (`useInstallableConnectorCatalog`) joined with connection groups
   (`useConnectionConnectorGroups`), filtered to `installed || connection_count > 0`;
2. `buildInferenceConnectorRows(inferenceProviders)` → synthetic rows keyed `inference:{slug}`;
3. `buildSandboxConnectorRows(sandboxes)` → synthetic rows keyed `sandbox:{id}`.

All three render as `<Link to="/$owner/connectors/$connectorKey">`; the detail page
(`$connectorKey.index.tsx`, ~1300 lines) branches on the key prefix and renders
`InferenceProviderDetail` / `SandboxDetail` / the real connector shell. Key prefixes are
constants in `@lobu/core/reserved` (`SANDBOX_ROW_KEY_PREFIX`, `SANDBOX_PROVIDER_KEY_PREFIX`,
`INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX`).

Facets (`lib/connectors/facets.ts`) drive 11 filter chips: all / data / chat / actions /
inference / runtime / oauth / api_key / app_install / device ("On device") / needs_setup.
`ConnectionFacets` = `{data, chat, actions, audience, inference, runtime}`. `device` is NOT a
facet — it is derived via `connectorIsDeviceBound(connector)` = `!!connector.runtime ||
!!connector.required_capability`.

The catalog picker (`components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-form.tsx`) composes the
same three families for `/connectors/create`, including
`buildSandboxProviderCatalogEntries(availableProviders)` → `sandbox-provider:{kind}` entries
whose click handler sets `selectedSandboxKind` and swaps in a locked create form — i.e. a
catalog entry that is NOT a connector and opens a bespoke panel is an established pattern.

### Devices

`device_workers` table. Registered in `packages/server/src/worker-api/poll.ts:256` — an upsert on
`(user_id, worker_id)` on every user-scoped worker poll. Columns used here: `user_id`,
`worker_id`, `platform`, `app_version`, `capabilities`, `label`, `organization_id`,
`connector_manifests`, `last_seen_at`. `platform` is set-once (COALESCE) as a security measure.

`packages/core/src/capabilities.ts` `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST` has exactly three platforms:
`macos`, `ios`, `chrome-extension`. A poll with any other platform (or none) gets its declared
capabilities dropped to `[]`. **`cli` / `node` is not a platform** — the Lobu CLI never creates a
`device_workers` row. The Docker bridge (`packages/connector-worker`) sends no platform, so it
can register a row but advertises zero capabilities.

`GET /api/me/devices` (`worker-api/device-management.ts:40`) is **user-scoped and cross-org**:
`WHERE dw.user_id = ${userId}`, returning each device's `organization_id`/`organization_slug`,
`connector_count`, `connector_error_count`, `last_sync_at`, and the array of pinned connections.
`online` = `last_seen_at > now() - interval '20 minutes'`.

Device → connectors: `worker-api/device-reconcile.ts` `reconcileDeviceCapabilities` /
`ensureDeviceConnectorWired` install a bundled device connector definition, a no-auth connection,
and the first feed into the user's org for each capability the fresh device fleet advertises, and
auto-pin `connections.device_worker_id` when exactly one fresh device qualifies. So a paired Mac
ALREADY materializes Screen Time / Photos / Calendar / Reminders / computer_use rows in the
connectors list today.

Device detail route `runtime/devices/$deviceId.tsx` is 404 lines: rename (`PATCH
/api/me/devices/:id`), delete (`DELETE`, which tombstones device pins via
`utils/device-pin-tombstones.ts`), a `RunsPanel`, capability chips (`CAPABILITY_LABELS`), auth
profiles, and links back to pinned connections.

### MCP clients

`GET /api/:orgSlug/clients` (`packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts:210`) returns
`oauth_clients` rows for the org, mapped to `ConnectedClientItem` plus messaging clients
(`kind: "messaging"`). `DELETE /mcp/:clientId?scope=all` revokes.

`apps.tsx` filters to `kind === "mcp"` and groups by server-provided `registrationGroupKey`
(`JSON.stringify([client_name, owner_user_id, organizationId])`) because a client that
re-registers creates a new row under the same name. `groupClients()` is exported FROM the route
file and imported by `lib/group-clients.test.ts`. `kind: "messaging"` clients are fetched and
rendered nowhere.

**Known identity defect (measured on prod 2026-07-30):** `client-routes.ts:258` computes
`title = clientInfo.name || client_name` — the per-session `initialize` clientInfo WINS over the
DCR registration name. Result: 5 of 19 prod rows display a different vendor than they registered
as — `Owletto for Mac → claude-code` (x3), `Lobu CLI → claude-code`, `Claude → claude-code`.
`isFirstPartyLobuClient(title, softwareId)` (`client-routes.ts:56`) therefore evaluates FALSE for
the real Lobu first-party clients, because `title` is "claude-code" and `software_id` is NULL on
all 19 prod rows. `client-session-routes.ts` joins `oauth_clients.client_name` — the opposite
precedence, so the two surfaces disagree.

`metadata.last_agent_id` is NULL on all 19 prod rows, so the `agentId` filter at
`client-routes.ts:255` drops every client from any agent-scoped view.

### Entry points that must be repointed (grepped, excluding routeTree.gen)

To `/connectors/runtime` or `/runtime/devices/$deviceId`:
- `app/index.tsx:107` — hand-built URL string
- `app/$owner/connectors/$connectorKey.index.tsx:1080`, `:1241`
- `components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-form.tsx:781`, `:1413` ("Add device")
- `components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-settings-tab.tsx:450`
- `components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-feed-detail.tsx:83`
- `components/devices/devices-body.tsx:47`
- `components/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:471` (user menu "My devices")
- `app/__smoke__/all-routes.test.tsx:204,205,217,218`

To `/connectors/apps`:
- `components/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:485` (user menu "Connected apps")
- `components/home/client-sessions-timeline.tsx:63`
- `app/__smoke__/all-routes.test.tsx:210,211`
- `lib/group-clients.test.ts:2`

## Proposed design

### 1. Devices become `device:{id}` rows in the connectors list

New `lib/connectors/device-rows.ts` mirroring `sandbox-rows.ts` exactly:
`buildDeviceConnectorRows(devices)` → `{connector, facets, device}` with
`connector.key = "device:{id}"`, `name = deviceName(device)`,
`status = device.online ? "active" : "error"`, facets `{runtime: true}` (rest false).

Rationale for `runtime` rather than a new facet: a paired Mac is the local counterpart of a
remote sandbox — the sandbox lede already says sandboxes are where agents execute "instead of
the built-in local runtime". Sandboxes are already `runtime`-faceted rows in this list.

Row meta line: `macOS · 5 connectors · online` / `offline 2h`.
`needsSetup` = false (a device with no capabilities is not "unconfigured", it is a device).

Detail: `$connectorKey.index.tsx` gains a `device:` branch rendering a `DeviceDetail` component
extracted verbatim from today's `runtime/devices/$deviceId.tsx` body. Route
`/$owner/connectors/runtime/*` is deleted; `/$owner/connectors/device:{id}` is the new home.

### 2. MCP clients become `client:{groupKey}` rows in the connectors list

`buildClientConnectorRows(clientGroups)` from the existing `groupClients()` output (moved to
`lib/clients/group-clients.ts` so a route file stops exporting logic).
`connector.key = "client:{groupKey}"` — NOTE `registrationGroupKey` is a JSON array string
containing `"` and `,`; it must be URL-encoded into the route param and decoded back.
Row meta: `Burak Emre · active 3m ago` / `disconnected`.

New facet needed: none of the six `ConnectionFacets` fit ("what an app can do for your agent" is
the wrong axis for an inbound client). Proposal: add a 12th filter chip `client` ("Apps") that
matches on the key prefix rather than on a facet, keeping `ConnectionFacets` unchanged.

Detail: a `client:` branch in `$connectorKey.index.tsx` rendering identity (registered name,
driven-by clientInfo, redirect_uris host, software id/version), linked user, last seen, active
token count, sessions, and Revoke (admin-only, already `withOrgAdmin`-gated server-side).

### 3. Install recipes move into the catalog

`components/devices/device-connect.tsx` today is four stateless accordions (macOS app → "Contact
us" link; Chrome extension → web store link; CLI → `npm i -g @lobu/cli && lobu login && lobu
memory configure --url {mcpUrl}`; Docker → `docker run …`). These become catalog entries
`install:{id}` in the `/connectors/create` picker, using the `sandbox-provider:` mechanic: click
sets state and swaps in an instructions panel instead of a form.

Same family gains MCP-client recipes (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex) built from
`buildMcpUrl(orgSlug)` — the GUI form of what `lobu memory configure --url` does today.

"Add device" CTAs (`connection-form.tsx:1413`, `connection-settings-tab.tsx:450`) repoint from
the devices LIST to `/connectors/create` filtered to these entries — i.e. they now land on
instructions, which is what they wanted in the first place.

### 4. Client identity fix (server)

`client-routes.ts`: `title` becomes `client_name` (DCR registration) with `clientInfo.name`
demoted to a new `drivenBy` field. `isFirstPartyLobuClient` keys off `client_name` +
`redirect_uris` host. This is a prerequisite for (2) and (5) — without it, the three Lobu
first-party surfaces all label themselves "claude-code" in prod.

### 5. Device/client de-duplication

The Owletto Mac app creates BOTH a `device_workers` row AND an `oauth_clients` row; there is no
FK between the tables. Without a rule it appears twice in the merged list. Proposed rule: a
first-party client row is suppressed when a `device:` row exists for the same
`(owner_user_id, platform)`. Depends on (4) for a trustworthy platform signal.

### 6. Scoping (OPEN — reviewer should attack this)

`/connectors` is org-scoped. `GET /api/me/devices` is user-scoped and cross-org. Proposed v1:
filter client-side to `device.organization_id === current org`. Consequence: a teammate's paired
Mac is invisible even though `ensureDeviceConnectorWired` may have wired its connectors into an
org you can see. Proper fix (deferred): an org-scoped device endpoint with owner attribution,
admin-only delete, owner-only rename.

### 7. Redirects

`/connectors/runtime` → `/connectors`; `/connectors/runtime/devices/$deviceId` →
`/connectors/device:{id}`; `/connectors/apps` → `/connectors`. Repo precedent exists
(`/environments` → `/connectors`, `memory/memory-legacy-redirects.test.tsx`). Note repo rule
"no backwards-compat shims" — argued as not applicable to bookmarkable user-facing URLs.

### 8. Ship shape

ONE PR (user's explicit instruction), covering: server identity fix + device rows + client rows +
two detail branches + catalog install recipes + deletion of 4 route files + 12 repointed call
sites + redirects + tests.

## Questions for the reviewer

1. Is putting an inbound MCP client (a thing that calls INTO Lobu with a person's access) in the
   same list as outbound connectors (things an agent reaches OUT to) a category error that will
   cost more than the page it saves? A prior session's adversarial review rejected exactly this
   for a Runtime tab and instead decided MCP clients are "external agents" belonging on the
   Agents page. The user has now overruled that. What breaks?
2. Revoking a client's grant and deleting an org connection are different danger classes on one
   page. Is prefix-branching the detail page enough separation, or does the LIST need it?
3. Is `runtime` the right facet for a device, given a device is BOTH a runtime and a source of
   connectors (whose provided connectors already appear as their own rows)?
4. Section 6 scoping: is the client-side org filter honest, or does it under-report in a way that
   makes the merged list wrong?
5. Section 5 de-dup: is suppression right, or should the two identities be linked properly?
6. Is ONE PR defensible here, or does the server-side identity fix (independently
   prod-verifiable, different blast radius, different rollback) have to be split out?
7. What did this design miss — specifically in `$connectorKey.index.tsx`'s existing prefix
   branching, the `connection_count`/`needsSetup` sort invariants, and the catalog picker's
   `installedOnly` mode?

Design doc is written and the Fable review is running against the real source. While it works, here's the answer to your question 3 — what an MCP client row opens into.

**`client:{client_id}` → a detail page that answers "what has this app actually been doing with my workspace?"** All the data already exists server-side:

- **Identity** — registered name (`client_name`), *driven by* (`clientInfo.name`, e.g. `claude-code`), redirect host (`chatgpt.com`), software id/version, and the person it authenticates as. These are the six signals in `oauth_clients`; today the row shows one of them and picks the wrong one.
- **Sessions** — `GET /clients/sessions` (`client-session-routes.ts`) already returns per-session `call_count`, `failed_count`, `tools[]`, `pending_interaction_count` over a 14-day window. It's currently only consumed by the Home timeline (`client-sessions-timeline.tsx`), which links to the page we're deleting. Filtered to one client, that's the meat of the detail page: *ChatGPT · 498 run_sdk · 123 query_sql · 3 failed*.
- **Activity trail** — `events.client_id` is the only per-invocation identity signal, and the server already accepts `client_ids` on read. The owletto-side `event-filters.ts` gap is ~40 lines, so "see everything this app touched" becomes a real deep-link into `/activity`.
- **Revoke** — existing `DELETE /mcp/:clientId?scope=all`, admin-gated server-side.

One correction to my own doc I'll make regardless of what the review says: the route param should be `client:{client_id}`, not the group key. `registrationGroupKey` is a JSON array string (`["Claude","usr_…","org_…"]`) — quotes, commas and brackets in a URL segment. Use the group's primary client id and re-derive the group on the detail page.

Side benefit: the Home timeline's session rows stop pointing at an inventory page and start pointing at the specific app that made those calls.

I'll bring you the review findings when they land — particularly on whether one PR holds together and whether the inbound/outbound merge survives scrutiny.

Approved design, **not yet built**. Grew out of "why don't I see Recent?" →
[[project_dm_conversation_visibility]] → the archived-Behaviors bug.

## The rule this obeys

New AGENTS.md hard invariant (committed on `feat/behavior-listing-rows`):
**request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY` / `DISTINCT ON` /
per-row `regexp_*` / leading-wildcard `LIKE` over `events`,
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls` on a user-facing read path.
Materialize at WRITE time; run the one-time aggregation in a migration.
Bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`,
`oauth_clients`) are fine to aggregate.

Two known violations: `agent-thread-list.ts` (being fixed, see
[[project_behavior_listing_column]]) and `client-session-routes.ts:76`
(`GROUP BY metadata->>'mcp_session_id'` over `current_event_records`) — PR 2.

## Contract

```
GET /lobu/api/v1/workspace/recent
  ?filter=web|slack|telegram|whatsapp|discord|behavior|client   repeatable; omit ⇒ all
  &agentId=<id>    repeatable; omit ⇒ all agents
  &limit=20 (max 100)  &cursor=<keyset on (lastActivityAt, id)>
```

Payload uses TWO fields — **`type` says what the row is, `platform` says which
external surface, null when there isn't one.** `platform` alone was rejected
("behavior is not a platform"); `trigger`/`origin`/`kind`/`source` were all
rejected as already-taken (see below).

```jsonc
{ "type": "conversation", "platform": "slack", "conversationId": "slack:D095…" }
{ "type": "conversation", "platform": "web",   "threadId": "mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5" }
{ "type": "behavior",     "platform": null,    "behaviorId": 71 }
{ "type": "client",       "platform": null,    "clientId": "mcp_client_8hOPs3…" }
```

Server resolves the flat filter as `type === 'conversation' ? platform : type`.
Response also carries `counts` per filter value — chips need totals, and a
truncated page gives wrong ones.

**Name collisions that forced `type`** (all verified in-repo/prod):
`trigger` = `watchers.triggers`; `origin` = `events.origin_type`, a
connector-owned open set with **84 distinct values in prod**; `kind` =
`conversations.kind` (owned/platform); `source` = `watchers.sources`.

## SQL shape

Four branches, `UNION ALL`, **each with its own `LIMIT $n`** so the union is at
most 4n rows regardless of table size; outer `ORDER BY … LIMIT $n`.
`conversations_listing` already indexes `(org, agent, last_activity_at DESC)
WHERE archived_at IS NULL`; `oauth_clients` is 19 rows.

**Trap:** the channel ACL fence is applied in TS today (`isConversationVisible`).
With per-branch LIMIT that under-fills the page and makes `counts.platform`
wrong. Resolve visible channel keys first (bounded), pass them into the platform
branch as a `text[]` predicate — and that needs `pgTextArray`, see
[[feedback_pg_array_any_fetch_types]].

## Also exposed via run_sdk

`client.workspace.recent({ filter?, agent_id?, limit, cursor })`, read access,
same union behind both surfaces. Today only `client.conversations.list({agent_id})`
exists — conversations only, per agent, can't answer "recent activity".

## `/connectors/apps` gets deleted

Its list is redundant once `client` rows exist. **But it is the ONLY consumer of
`useRevokeMcpClient` in the SPA** — deleting it naively removes the sole way to
disconnect ChatGPT/Claude. Decision: Revoke moves into the **conversation view's
composer slot** — `agent-thread.tsx:145` already branches
`readOnly ? footer : <ChatComposer/>`, so a client-attribution panel ("this
conversation is from ChatGPT" + info + Revoke) drops into that existing slot.
Requires conversation→client attribution first, see
[[reference_mcp_client_identity_and_attribution]].

Inbound refs to sweep before deleting: `app-sidebar.tsx:419` (nav item),
`client-sessions-timeline.tsx:63` (link), `all-routes.test.tsx`, and
`group-clients.test.ts` which imports `groupClients` from the route file.
Docs/help text not yet swept.

## Client rows must NOT be recency-sorted with everything else

`oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is bumped on EVERY authenticated MCP
request (`touchClientActivity`), so a connected client is permanently the newest
thing in the workspace — measured live: Claude 17:43, ChatGPT 17:10 while
working. Plain recency sorting would let 19 client rows sit at the top forever
and squeeze conversations out — the "Behaviors drown everything" failure, but
continuous. **DECIDED: clients get their own capped section (~3 rows); they do
not compete in the main recency ordering.**

## conversations.client_id — DROPPED, with an expiry condition

Dropped 2026-07-30. A Lobu conversation is a conversation with a LOBU AGENT.
When ChatGPT calls `conversations.send` there is no ChatGPT content in the row —
just the prompt it passed and the agent's reply. Labelling it "from ChatGPT"
claims more than the data supports, `user_id` already records the owning Lobu
user, and `events.client_id` already carries per-invocation attribution at the
correct grain (a conversation can be touched by several clients).

**Revisit when the inference proxy / SDK starts populating external clients'
own transcripts** (user's plan, 2026-07-30). Once a conversation actually
contains the client's turns, `client_id` stops being a mislabel and the
composer-slot attribution panel becomes accurate again. Until then Revoke lives
on a **client detail view** reached from the `client` row, NOT in the
conversation composer slot — that earlier plan depended on client_id.

## Ordering

1. [[project_behavior_listing_column]] — prerequisite, unblocked.
2. `conversations.client_id` attribution.
3. `/workspace/recent` + `client.workspace.recent`.
4. SPA switches Recent to it; `/connectors/apps` deleted in the SAME PR so the
   page and its replacement land together.
5. PR 2 — `client-session-routes.ts` de-aggregation.

content.text:
Right on both counts, and the first one is already decided — I should have caught it before proposing the sessions panel.

## Client sessions belong in Recent

There's an approved design from yesterday (`/lobu/api/v1/workspace/recent`) that unions conversations + behaviors + **clients** into one feed with `type` + nullable `platform`. It already says `/connectors/apps` gets deleted, and it already worked out the trap: `oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is bumped on *every* authenticated MCP request, so a connected client is permanently the newest thing in the workspace — Claude and ChatGPT would sit at the top of a recency-sorted feed forever. Decision there was a capped ~3-row client section that doesn't compete in the main ordering.

The reconciliation with what we're building isn't a conflict, it's a split I collapsed by accident:

- **Recent** answers *what happened* — sessions, calls, time-ordered. `type: "client"` rows.
- **Connectors** answers *what's connected* — registered, connected/disconnected, who granted it, revoke. Config inventory, not history.
- The `client:{id}` detail page is the join: one page, reached from either. That's normal.

The concrete consequence for our PR: **don't build the sessions panel on `client-session-routes.ts`.** That endpoint does `GROUP BY metadata->>'mcp_session_id'` over `events` (`client-session-routes.ts:76`), which violates the hard invariant now committed on `origin/main` (AGENTS.md:14 — "request paths never aggregate history"). It's already slated for de-aggregation. So our PR ships identity + status + linked person + revoke against `oauth_clients` (19 rows, a bounded config table — explicitly fine to aggregate), and the sessions panel arrives with Recent rather than being built twice.

## Why there are many API surfaces

Measured, not theorized: each page grew its own bespoke rollup over the same append-only `events` table.

`clients/sessions` (MCP session rollup), `activity` (event feed), `runs`, `behaviors`, `deployments` (5 separate `FROM events`), `metric-series`, agent thread lists — plus `clients` for inventory. Nine `lib/api/*` modules on the SPA side for what is largely one question asked with different `WHERE` clauses.

Nobody designed that; it's what happens when a page needs a number and the cheapest path is a new endpoint that computes it. The invariant on `origin/main` is the fix being applied going forward — materialize at write time, read by index — and two known violators are already tagged: `client-session-routes.ts` and `agent-thread-list.ts`. `/workspace/recent` is the consolidation for the feed half of it.

I'd rather not widen this PR to chase that; the honest scope is: our PR must not *add* a tenth surface or build on a doomed one. It doesn't have to fix the nine.

The Fable design review is still running against the source — I'll fold this into what it comes back with.

Review target: `the architecure as much as possible`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text:
`/simplify` normally reviews a diff; there isn't one yet, so I ran its four lenses over the architecture. The findings are mostly one finding.

## The real problem: six hand-rolled families where there should be one mechanism

The connectors list already synthesizes three non-connector row families — `inference-provider:`, `sandbox:`, `sandbox-provider:` (constants at `packages/core/src/reserved.ts:138,147,155`). Each one is the same six pieces copy-pasted: a prefix constant, a `build*Rows()`, a `parse*Key()`, an `is*Key()`, a branch in the list's `useMemo`, and **two** more in the detail route — a loader guard (`$connectorKey.index.tsx:150-151`) and a render branch (`:177-178`). Every family also fabricates a 12-field fake `ConnectorDefinitionItem` with an `as` cast to satisfy a type it isn't.

My design added three more (`device:`, `client:`, `install:`). That takes it from 3 copies to 6, and pushes a 1300-line detail route toward 1600. That's the special-case-on-shared-infrastructure smell, and going from 3 to 6 is exactly the "fix the class, not the instance" trigger.

**Replace it with one row-kind registry.** A kind declares: prefix, how to fetch its rows, how to map one to the small thing the list renders (key, name, icon, meta, facets, status), its detail component, and optionally its catalog entries. The list maps over the registry; the detail route resolves kind-by-prefix and renders `kind.Detail`.

Two constraints that keep it honest:
- **Unify dispatch, not rendering.** Real connectors have tabs, a rail, connections; a sandbox is a credential and a name. `kind.Detail` is just a component slot — the big one stays big, flat ones stay flat.
- **Invert the fake-connector cast.** The registry's row type is what the list actually renders, and real connectors adapt *into* it. Right now everything pretends to be a connector, which is why every family needs an `as`.

Adding devices and clients then costs two registry entries instead of twelve mechanisms, and the three existing families collapse into it — net deletion.

## Four smaller cuts that fall out

**`install:` isn't a family, it's the catalog half of kinds that already exist.** The `device` kind declares its catalog entries (Mac / Chrome / CLI / Docker recipes), the `client` kind declares its own (Claude Code / Cursor / ChatGPT). Same mechanism. This also lets `sandbox-provider:` be **deleted** — it's `sandbox`'s catalog, split into a second family for no reason. Six families become five kinds, one of which is real connectors.

**No 12th filter chip.** There are 11 already; clients are ~3 rows. Don't add `client`.

**Fix the loading gate while we're in there.** `index.tsx:122-126` ORs six queries into one `isContentLoading` — the whole list sits behind a skeleton until the slowest resolves. Adding devices (four correlated subqueries plus a lateral, per device) and clients (an `agents` join) makes that visibly worse. With a registry each kind renders when its own query lands; connectors paint immediately.

**State the dedup as a rule, not a heuristic.** The Mac creates both a `device_workers` row and an `oauth_clients` row. Rather than "suppress first-party clients matching a device platform": *a device's own OAuth client is plumbing, not a connected app.* One filter, and it still needs the `client_name`-over-`clientInfo` identity fix underneath it.

## If you want less work rather than better structure

The droppable piece is the client **detail page**. Devices-as-rows is well-founded on its own (a paired Mac is the local counterpart of a sandbox, which is already a `runtime`-faceted row). Clients could stay as plain rows with a revoke button at the bottom of `/connectors` — no route, no registry entry, ~30 lines moved out of `apps.tsx`. That's roughly a quarter of the work and still deletes both pages. It costs you the "click to see what this app has been doing", which is the part you asked for — so I'd only take it if the PR is running long.

---

Fable's independent review of the design is still running (codex is quota-dead until Aug 5 — that's the single-point-of-failure my notes flag, worth fixing separately). I'll reconcile its findings with this before any code.

**Confidence: high (85)** that the registry is the right call — I counted the actual duplication sites rather than inferring them (`reserved.ts:138/147/155`, `$connectorKey.index.tsx:150,151,177,178`, two `build*Rows` files at 92 and 136 lines). **Medium (55)** on effort: I haven't measured how much of `$connectorKey.index.tsx`'s 1300 lines is real-connector-specific versus genuinely shared, and that determines whether the registry is a clean extraction or a fight.

Next actions:
1. Wait for the Fable review and reconcile — it may kill the client-rows-under-connectors idea outright.
2. Let me measure the detail route: how much is connector-specific vs shared. That's the one number gating the registry's cost.
3. Decide registry-refactor-included vs the smaller cut, given the single-PR constraint.
4. Separately: `make review` has no working reviewer until Aug 5 unless `REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable` is made the default — worth fixing before this PR needs its required `pi-review` check.
